query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small percentage of rare-earth elements into the single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloy will increase the coercive field beyond 100 Oe.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloy with low coercive field (≤ 100 Oe).
generation.intervention: Addition of rare-earth elements (e.g., Yttrium or Neodymium) at a concentration of 1-5 atomic percent.
generation.conditions: Synthesis of the modified alloy under controlled conditions to ensure homogeneity and phase stability; magnetic measurements conducted at room temperature.
generation.structural_mediator: Changes in the magnetic anisotropy due to the presence of rare-earth elements.
generation.mechanism: Rare-earth elements are known to enhance magnetic anisotropy, which can lead to an increase in coercivity by stabilizing the magnetic domains against external magnetic fields.
generation.predicted_outcome: The coercive field of the modified alloy will exceed 100 Oe, potentially reaching values around 200 Oe or higher.
generation.baseline: Coercive field of single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloy is ≤ 100 Oe.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is limited to the specific range of rare-earth element concentrations (1-5 atomic percent) and the single-phase fcc structure of the alloy.
generation.uncertainty: The exact increase in coercivity is uncertain and may vary based on the specific rare-earth element used and its interaction with the alloy matrix.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloys with varying concentrations of rare-earth elements (1-5 atomic percent) and measure their coercive fields using a vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM).
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If all synthesized alloys with rare-earth additions show coercive fields ≤ 100 Oe, the hypothesis is falsified.
